column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/crossplane-function-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THE WORKFLOW IS. A `workflow_call` reusable AUTO-RELEASE: on a consumer's
# push to main it builds a Crossplane composition-Function's Nix runtime image,
# embeds it in an xpkg, and pushes that xpkg to an OCI registry (ghcr.io by
# default). Two jobs. `resolve` has NO `if:` and so always selects; `publish`
# needs it and carries the file's ONLY condition.
# WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 graphql-synthesizer ran cargo-auto-release,
# reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published nothing — its `ship`
# job carries `&& !github.event.repository.private` and the repo was private.
# The condition was correct. What was missing is that nobody had written down
# which jobs must run for a given input, so a deliberate no-publish and a broken
# no-publish were the same green tick. This file writes it down for this member
# of the release family.
# THE FINDING FOR THIS WORKFLOW, AND ROW 2 IS IT. This workflow does carry
# `github.event.repository.private` — three times — but NOT ONE of them is in an
# `if:`. All three sit in `runs-on:` and in the runner-resolve `default:` input:
# here the private signal ROUTES THE RUNNER (private -> camelot-builder-pleme-eks,
# public -> ubuntu-24.04/ubuntu-latest); it does not gate publishing. That is the
# right posture for this family — an xpkg is pushed to the consumer repo's own
# GHCR namespace, which inherits the repo's visibility, so there is no
# crates.io-style public-index leak to prevent, and a private Function repo is
# expected to keep shipping. So the mandatory "private + bump -> publish skips"
# row of the sweep INVERTS here: on a private repo `publish` MUST STILL RUN.
# Row 2 asserts exactly that. If anyone ever copies cargo-auto-release's
# `&& !github.event.repository.private` guard onto `publish`, row 2 turns
# NOT-RUN and names the job instead of going quietly green.
# THE REAL GATE IS THE ACTOR, AND ROW 3 IS IT. `publish`'s whole condition is
# `github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'` — the anti-self-retrigger guard. A
# bot-authored push selects `resolve` and nothing else. That is a DELIBERATE
# no-publish, and row 3 is where it is now written down as one rather than
# inferred from a green run.
# NO BUMP JOB, SO NO NO-BUMP CASE. Version selection is not a job here: the tag
# is computed inside `publish`'s "Resolve tag" step (explicit `inputs.tag`, else
# `sha-<short>` off the merge commit). There is no bumped/not-bumped fork in the
# job graph to assert, so the sweep's third mandatory case has no subject. Row 4
# pins the other input axis instead — the on-demand semver path via a caller's
# workflow_dispatch selects the same two jobs as a merge push, i.e. the semver
# release is not a separate reachability story.
# KEY SET. Every row declares the same four keys. Only `github.actor` is read by
# a condition today; `github.event.repository.private`, `github.event_name` and
# `inputs.tag` are declared deliberately so that a future `if:` reading any of
# them evaluates into a NAMED assertion failure rather than an undeclared-path
# error. This is a called reusable, so `github.event_name` is the CALLER's event
# and `inputs.tag` is its `workflow_call` input. An empty value models "not
# supplied", which is the documented default of `tag`. No status function
# (always/success/failure/cancelled) appears anywhere in this workflow, so none
# is supplied.
# 1. The nominal path: a human merge to a PUBLIC consumer's main publishes.
public-push-publishes
# 2. THE ROW THE SWEEP EXISTS FOR, INVERTED. Private repo, and publish MUST run:
#    the privacy signal in this workflow routes the runner, it does not gate the
#    push. A NOT-RUN here means someone added a privacy publish-guard.
private-push-still-publishes
# 3. The one deliberate no-publish in this workflow, stated as such: the bot must
#    not re-trigger its own pushes. `resolve` is unconditional and still selects.
bot-push-no-self-retrigger
# 4. On-demand semver via the caller's workflow_dispatch: same selection as a
#    merge push. Pins that the explicit-tag path is not a separate job graph.
dispatch-explicit-semver-tag
